blind.why: Full locker at 1920x1080 (fresh_1920_t3) vs the CS2 loadout (ss_13). CS2 shows both team agents and the real in-game models, a dense 5x3 loadout and two full rows of the inventory grid with rarity underlines. Ours gives about 60% of the screen to one stand-in figure on an empty stage, shows only one row of items, and the 3D 'YOU' nameplate sits behind the EMBER/TIDE toggle and reads as 'TOU'.

1280x720 tagger-skins tab (tide_skin) vs the CS2 loadout scaled to 1280. Ours has layout collisions: the SPIN/FULL/HEAD toolbar sits over the 'No Trail' kit row and the emote card, the share code field collapses to zero width so the code is hidden, 'COPY' and 'APPLY' run together as 'COPYAPPLY', 'LOADOUT 1' wraps, the tab bar cuts off at 'TA' with no scroll cue, and only one row of items is visible above the bottom bar. CS2's layout is clean at the same size.

Cosmetics in game at 4.5 m (game_close: Ember in Neon Drift and Abyssal, Tide in Solar and Neon) vs CS2 agents (ss_1). The teams do read (Ember is orange/red, Tide is blue), but the cosmetics disappear: the Neon Drift suit, black and magenta in the locker, becomes an orange body in game. Both teams wear purple helmets, and every figure is the same rigid robot. CS2 agents are individually recognisable and the team still reads.

biggest_gap: The locker preview is not what you get in game. The preview is a stand-in blocky rig with the raw suit colours. In game, characters.refreshCosmetics recolours the suit to the team: an Ember player who equips Neon Drift Skin (shown black and magenta in the locker, random_2_ember.png) or Abyssal Skin (shown teal) plays as an orange/peach body (game_close.png, actors 0 and 1). Meanwhile resolve() leaves most suits identical across teams (suit.base for neon, void, midnight, tide-ii, verdant, gilded, chrome, solar and lantern is byte-identical for ember and tide). So the team guard lives in characters and the locker never shows it. Repro: ?scene=locker, equip suit-neon on Ember, then compare with createActor({team:'ember'}) plus setLoadout/apply in ?test=1&seed=1. CS2's loadout renders the actual agent model, so what you see is what you play. Fix: render the preview with the real in-game character (characters.createPreview) and team tint. Show each suit card already tinted to the active side, and design suits as team-banded variants (Ember and Tide versions), so the 'skin' survives in game.
other_gaps: 720p layout breaks: the toolbar overlaps the kit lists, the share code field has zero width, 'COPY' and 'APPLY' collide, the tab bar is truncated, 'SAVE & EQUIP' is clipped at the right edge (random_2_ember), the 'RANDOMISED' toast covers the side toggle, and the item grid shows 0.85 rows. Collapse the side panels or shrink the stage at heights of 800 px or less.
The item grid is starved at every size: 10 cards at 1080p and 6 at 720p, so browsing 20 suits needs a blind scroll. CS2 shows 16+ items. Give the grid at least two full rows and shrink the stage.
The 3D 'YOU' nameplate floats above the figure's head and renders behind the EMBER/TIDE toggle ('TOU'). Lower it or hide it outside the nameplate tab.

Cosmetic identity is weak in game: helmets and visors are the only parts that survive, both teams can wear the same magenta Neon helmet, and trails and charms are not rendered in game, so roughly 4 of 11 categories are invisible to opponents.
Card icons are flat front-on 2D figures. The suit cards are the same mannequin recoloured, and tagger skins are all the same rifle silhouette. CS2 item art is 3/4 lit renders with depth.
Share codes are lossy: decode(encode(l)) changes skinWear from 0.030 to 0.02857, so the shared float differs from the one shown ('FACTORY FRESH · 0.030').
bugs: Share code roundtrip not identity (skinWear quantised: 0.03 -> 0.028571)
3D 'YOU' nameplate occluded by/overlapping EMBER/TIDE toggle in default view (all sizes)
1280x720: toolbar overlaps kit rows; share code input zero-width; COPY/APPLY overlap; 'SAVE & EQU' clipped off-screen
Intermittent empty item grid on first suit tab capture (locker_sheet ember_suit.png at 1280x720; not reproduced on retry)
Ember can equip Tide set's 'Abyssal Skin' (suit-tide-ii) and Neon Drift whose locker preview contradicts in-game team-tinted look
strengths: Large, coherent catalog: 154 items in 11 categories and 9 sets, with a sensible rarity spread (32 common, 57 rare, 43 epic, 22 legendary) and a CS2-faithful rarity colour language (grey, blue, magenta, gold underlines)
Good CS2 nods: a wear float bar ('FACTORY FRESH 0.030'), finish tags (SATIN, METALLIC), a hover-to-inspect preview with a flavour-text tooltip, and a Sets tab with progress per set
Persistence works: equip, Ctrl+S, reload and the loadout is identical; localStorage holds 4 slots for each side
Team read survives at 15 to 30 m even with the worst-case suits (fixes the avatars-r1 complaint in game); no console errors from cosmetics
Turntable stage with team-coloured lighting, view presets (full, head, back, tagger), tag-out and emote playback
